Tidying the results of other network models

Source: R/report_models.R
other_results.Rd

tidy() and glance() give the results of other packages' network models as a tibble, after {broom}, with the same columns as for a netreg (see netreg_results) where they mean the same. So an MRQAP result can sit in one table beside an ERGM or a SIENA one. They cover:

  • netlm and netlogit, from net_regression() in {migraph} before 2.0.0, which also have a print() method;

  • ergm, from ergm() in {ergm};

  • sienaFit, from siena07() in {RSiena}.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'netlm'
tidy(x, conf.int = FALSE, conf.level = 0.95, ...)

# S3 method for class 'netlogit'
tidy(x, conf.int = FALSE, conf.level = 0.95, exponentiate = FALSE, ...)

# S3 method for class 'netlm'
glance(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'netlogit'
glance(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'netlm'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'netlogit'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'ergm'
tidy(x, conf.int = FALSE, conf.level = 0.95, exponentiate = FALSE, ...)

# S3 method for class 'ergm'
glance(x, deviance = FALSE, mcmc = FALSE, ...)

# S3 method for class 'sienaFit'
tidy(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'sienaFit'
glance(x, ...)

Arguments

x

A netlm, netlogit, ergm, or sienaFit.

conf.int

Logical, whether to add the columns conf.low and conf.high.

conf.level

The level of the interval that conf.int adds.

...

Further arguments, passed to summary() for an ergm and otherwise not used.

exponentiate

Logical, whether to exponentiate the estimates, e.g. to give odds ratios for a logistic model.

deviance, mcmc

For an ergm, whether to add the deviance columns or the MCMC settings.

Value

tidy() and glance() return a tibble, and print() returns x, invisibly.

Details

For a {migraph} result, conf.int = TRUE adds the quantiles of the permuted test statistics. These describe the null distribution, not an interval around the estimate.

See also

Other models: control_mrqap(), diagnose_confusion(), play_diffusions(), print.netreg_lm(), regression, specify, specify_terms, terms_mrqap, test_fit, test_measures, test_parameter()

Examples

fit <- suppressMessages(
  ergm::ergm(manynet::as_network(manynet::ison_adolescents) ~ edges))
tidy(fit)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 6
#>   term  estimate std.error mcmc.error statistic p.value
#>   <chr>    <dbl>     <dbl>      <dbl>     <dbl>   <dbl>
#> 1 edges   -0.588     0.394          0     -1.49   0.136
glance(fit)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 5
#>   independence iterations logLik   AIC   BIC
#>   <lgl>             <int>  <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1 TRUE                  4  -18.2  38.5  39.8
